title: Inventory Sync v1
tagline: One source of truth for stock across the webstore, Shopee and Tokopedia.

summary.building: A sync service that records every stock movement in one ledger and pushes the result to all sales channels.
summary.so_that: We stop overselling: 38 orders were cancelled last month because the same unit sold on two channels.
summary.done_when: DoD-1 to DoD-5 verified; G1 and G2 checked 2 weeks after full rollout.
summary.biggest_risk: Year-end volume arrives before rollout ends. Mitigated by staged channel enablement (D-03) and buffer stock (D-04).
summary.now: Phase 1 of 4, Foundation. DoD-1 verified; 2 days over the original estimate.

business_context.problem: Ops updates stock by hand in each channel seller dashboard, twice a day, from a shared spreadsheet. Between updates, the last unit of a SKU can sell on two channels at once.

affected.impact: 3 people spend about 2 hours a day on manual stock edits.
38 orders were cancelled last month after payment.
Repeated cancellations risk reduced visibility or delisting.

business_context.why_now: Year-end sales run at roughly 3× normal volume starting December. At that volume the manual process breaks completely.

glossary.meaning: One sellable variant; stock is tracked per SKU.
Selling more units than physically available, forcing a cancellation.
Difference between ledger stock and channel stock.

goals_scope.goal: Ops and customers see the same stock on every channel within a minute, so the last unit never sells twice.

outcomes.check_on: 2 weeks after all channels are enabled

definition_of_done.condition: Ledger migrations apply and roll back cleanly on a staging copy of production data (`make migrate-roundtrip`).
definition_of_done.evidence: CI run 412 passed on 2026-10-18; log linked on the board card.

definition_of_done.condition: Replaying 30 days of recorded channel orders in shadow mode produces 0 unexplained drift rows (`python -m sync.replay --days 30`).
definition_of_done.verified_by: Replay job output, reviewed by the Ops lead

definition_of_done.condition: Technical release gates in technical-spec §10 pass.
definition_of_done.verified_by: Gate checklist in the technical spec, signed by the tech lead

definition_of_done.condition: All three channels are enabled per Section 8 and Ops has stopped editing the spreadsheet.
Runbook for drift alerts and rollback is handed to Ops on-call and walked through once.

modules.title: Stock ledger
modules.tldr: Every stock change is recorded in one place and reservations work on staging.
modules.delivers: Ledger and reservation API running on staging
modules.exit_criteria: DoD-1 verified; reservation API deployed to staging

modules.title: Channel adapters
modules.tldr: Orders from all three channels reach the ledger in shadow mode.
modules.delivers: Adapters for webstore, Shopee, and Tokopedia running in shadow mode
modules.depends_on: Marketplace API credentials from Ops; M1 on staging
modules.exit_criteria: DoD-2 replay passes for all three channels

modules.title: Push workers
modules.tldr: Channels receive updated stock within a minute without hitting rate limits.
modules.delivers: Push workers writing stock to channels in shadow mode
modules.depends_on: M1 on staging; buffer size from Q2
modules.exit_criteria: 7 days of shadow pushes with p95 lag ≤ 60 s

decisions.title: One warehouse in v1
decisions.tldr: v1 syncs stock for the main warehouse only.

fields.label: Why
fields.text: All channel stock ships from the main warehouse today.

fields.label: Cost
fields.text: The returns shelf stays on the spreadsheet until v2.

fields.label: Revisit if
fields.text: A second warehouse starts fulfilling channel orders.

decisions.title: Channel enablement order
decisions.tldr: Enable channels one at a time, lowest-risk first.

fields.label: Why
fields.text: A bad push on the webstore is reversible in minutes; a marketplace penalty is not.

options.title: Webstore, then Shopee, then Tokopedia
options.why: Each step proves the next; adds about 4 days to phase 3.

options.title: Enable all three together
options.why: Fastest, but one failure hits every channel during year-end ramp-up.

options.title: Marketplaces first
options.why: Fixes most oversells soonest, but tests first on the least forgiving channels.

decisions.title: Buffer stock per channel
decisions.tldr: Hide a few units per marketplace so sync delay cannot oversell the last unit.

fields.label: Cost
fields.text: A channel can show sold out while one unit remains.

phases.title: Spike
phases.delivers: Measured API limits and webhook behavior
phases.exit_criteria: Limits documented in the technical spec

phases.title: Channels
phases.delivers: M2 adapters and M3 workers in shadow mode
phases.exit_criteria: 7 days with p95 lag ≤ 60 s and no unexplained drift

phases.title: Rollout
phases.delivers: Reconciliation, admin view, and channel enablement
phases.exit_criteria: All channels enabled; ops retires spreadsheet

risks.risk: Year-end volume starts before phase 3 finishes
risks.mitigation: Freeze scope after phase 1; enable webstore first so the busiest channel is covered early

risks.risk: Ops keeps editing dashboards by hand after enablement
risks.mitigation: Remove dashboard stock-edit rights per channel at enablement; Ops lead signs DoD-4

assumptions.assumption: Both marketplaces allow stock updates at our seller tier.
Order volume stays below 10k/day for 6 months.

steps.label: Seed
steps.text: Import spreadsheet stock; diff every SKU before go-live.

steps.label: Shadow mode
steps.text: Compute and log pushes without writing channels.

steps.label: Flags
steps.text: Enable channels independently in the order chosen in D-03.

steps.label: Rollback
steps.text: Disable affected flag; ops resumes spreadsheet; ledger keeps recording.

rollout_rollback.point_of_no_return: Ops stops maintaining the spreadsheet, after 2 clean weeks and explicit sign-off.

open_questions.question: Who owns drift alerts after hand-over?

evidence.label: Gap
evidence.text: Ops on-call has no engineering access today; engineering on-call has no channel dashboard access.

options.title: Ops on-call, with an engineering escalation path
options.why: Ops can pause a channel flag immediately; needs a short runbook.

options.title: Engineering on-call
options.why: Can fix root causes, but cannot see channel dashboards today.

open_questions.question: How should channel buffer size be calculated?

evidence.label: Trade-off
evidence.text: Larger buffers prevent more oversells but hide sellable stock.

options.title: Fixed 2 units
options.why: Easy to explain and operate for v1.

guides.summary: Five jargon-free lines: build, business outcome, done-when by ID, biggest risk, current phase.
guides.goals_scope: Outcomes are measured later and never block delivery. Each DoD item is binary, names a verifier, and records evidence once verified. Typical set: functional acceptance, technical release gates, rollout complete, runbook handed over, owner sign-off.
guides.modules: Each workstream names an accountable owner, an observable delivery, dependencies, a checkable exit, and technical-spec IDs instead of technical detail.
guides.decisions: Plan decisions cover scope, ownership, budget, schedule, rollout, hosting or procurement, and process adoption. Technical choices go to the technical spec as TD.
guides.phases: Exit criteria must be independently checkable. Covers lists the DoD IDs each phase satisfies; every DoD item belongs to one phase.
guides.risks_assumptions: Plan risks cover adoption, staffing, timing, dependencies, approvals, and operational readiness. An unverified assumption past its verify-by date moves to the risk table.
guides.observability: Only metrics that track an outcome target. Technical metrics live in the technical spec.
guides.open_questions: Every question needs an owner, due date, blocked item, evidence, and actionable choices. Technical questions go to the technical spec as TQ.
